chapter: Europe, expatriates and The Loud Minority
title: Foster's group The Loud Minority
summary: Foster describes his undisciplined band with its soloists and women instrumentalists.

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you a question. Tell us a little bit about your group, The Loud Minority.

Ah, The Loud Minority. Undisciplined, unbridled passion, and rage — happy rage. That was the most undisciplined group of men and women. I had two ladies in and out of that band — and instrumentalists, not vocalists. I had male and female vocalists, but lady instrumentalists — Janice Robinson the trombonist, and Sharon Freeman, a French horn and pianist. But we were characterized by our inability to play soft, or for lorng. I didn’t plan it that way it just happened. And everybody was a soloist. We didn’t omit anybody from the solo category. And there were some who weren’t that proficient at soloing but I insisted that they just try to get it together. And there were even some who soloed on songs that they had no business playing on them. This one guy played trumpet. He should never have been playing “Shiny Stockings” but he did it, he played a solo in “Shiny Stockings” and every time he got [snaps fingers] this from the audience. Well, what can I do? I can’t take it away from him, but they would listen to my wife, Cecelia, but they wouldn’t listen to me. If I’d cuss them out, you know, I’d do the old Illinois Jacquet on them “y’all sounded like—y’all didn’t do the —” But one set they would get together and they would be perfectly together, and the next set, the unbridled, undisciplined rage would return.
That’s the first time I heard it put like that, Foss.
Yeah, I got several, I got a whole bunch of fugitives from The Loud Minority infiltrating the world out there. One of these days we’re going to take over.
